checks.quote: The format of these files is ######.yaml (where ###### is the launchpad bug number)
checks.note: Supported: filename format, required query key, optional suppress-graph, allow-nonvoting, test_ids, and core self-approval of single-query changes. Not confirmed from fetch: queries/ directory name, suppress-notification as a distinct key (only 'suppress ... graphs and notifications' via suppress-graph), and Lucene wording. Fetch tool returns summaries.

checks.quote: A rule of thumb is > 10% success hits probably means this isn't good enough.
checks.note: Also supported: fingerprint root cause, no hits on successful jobs, avoid wildcards, tags over filename, INFO+ only. 'Only documented false-positive control' / 'authoring time not match time' is the agent's interpretation, not stated.

checks.quote: this technique will only work on tempest or grenade jobs in the gate queue.
checks.note: test_ids and subunit2sql dependence confirmed. The 'too broad' narrowing description and the AND semantics were not separately surfaced in the fetch but are consistent.

checks.quote: Old queries which are no longer hitting in logstash are routinely deleted.
checks.note: Confirmed: --dry-run, 10 days no hits, re-assess, suppress-graph entries kept, Incomplete bug reopened, Future Work items 'check if any resolved bugs return' and nightly removal patch. Specific bug-status lists and elastic-recheck-cleanup Fix Committed/Released detail not individually quoted by fetch.

checks.quote: we found 7 days to be stable with 6TB of storage for 5TB effective with one replica on the old system.
checks.note: Supported: 7 days/6TB (clarkb), out of space last week (dpawlik, not fungi), 200MB logs, hosting/maintaining ER and logstash as next challenge, openstack-health stopped and repo retired, last commit 2021-05-19 with no archived notice. Attribution of out-of-space to fungi is wrong (dpawlik said it); 'sized for very large workload/maintenance burden' is interpretive.

checks.quote: the KCS article life cycle is non-linear.
checks.note: Supported: four states, Archived removed from search but viewable from linked incidents, archiving better than deleting, validated confidence sources, audience and governance fields, no retired state or numeric rule. Not confirmed: 'should exist only while incident is open' for WIP, 'restorable to any state'.

checks.quote: Start with one, keep it simple, and let our experience drive the need for additional templates.
checks.note: Template page supports Issue/Environment/Resolution/Cause(optional)/Metadata and no failed-approaches field; Environment wording is 'one of the key enablers in findability' not 'key factor'. Appendix E quick-reference claims could not be checked: the '...' path is truncated and guessed URLs (030/090, 030/030/020/090) returned 404 (UNREACHABLE for that part).

checks.quote: KCS articles that are flagged need to trigger a workflow that will get the attention of a subject matter expert.
checks.note: Reuse is Review: up to 80% rarely/never reused, 20% solve 80%, user responsible for quality; neither page defines metrics. Flag/fix confident-and-licensed rule confirmed. 'Never-referenced articles are never reviewed' is an inference.

checks.quote: we need to have link rates that exceed 60% and link accuracy that exceeds 90%.
checks.note: Supported: 60%/90% targets, accuracy more important, six checks, weight 2, below 90 coach, below 80 licence risk, PAR. Page calls it 'link rate/accuracy' in that quote; the Reuse Rate definition as percent of cases closed with article linked and the 'calibrated for staffed support orgs' remark were not surfaced.

checks.quote: a hyperlink embedded in a text field as part of an incident note would not satisfy this requirement.
checks.note: Technique 3.3 supported: many-to-many, optional type resolved/referenced, link/unlink, snapshot or specific version, link rate has no definition or target. 'Machine-usable' phrase not used verbatim. Glossary ('Linked') and Metrics Matrix (85% new etc.) could not be checked: the '...' paths are truncated and guesses returned 404 (UNREACHABLE for that part).
